section_1.title: Prerequisite Review: From Discrete to Continuous
section_1.content: Briefly recap discrete probability (bars). Transition to continuous variables where the probability of any exact point is zero, shifting the focus from 'height of a bar' to 'area under a curve'.
section_1.example: Comparing a histogram of test scores (discrete bars) to a smooth bell curve representing the same data distribution.

section_2.title: Defining the PDF
section_2.content: Introduce the PDF as a function f(x) where the area under the curve between two points equals the probability. Emphasize two rules: f(x) ≥ 0 and total area = 1.
section_2.example: Visualizing a 'Probability Fluid' being poured into a container—the total volume (area) must always equal 1 (100% certainty).

section_3.title: The Geometric Interpretation
section_3.content: Explain that finding the probability of a range [a, b] is equivalent to calculating the integral (area) under the curve between those bounds.
section_3.example: A robotic arm's precision: The PDF shows the likelihood of it landing in a specific 2cm zone; we calculate the shaded area to find the success rate.

section_4.title: Real-World Application: The Squirrel’s Acorn Search
section_4.content: Synthesize the knowledge: A squirrel drops an acorn. The PDF shows where it lands. We use the area under the curve to predict the squirrel's most likely hunting zone.
section_4.example: An animation showing a squirrel moving across an X-axis; the PDF curve spikes where the squirrel spends most of its time searching.

section_5.title: Summary & Key Takeaways
section_5.content: Recap: The PDF is not a probability itself, but a density. Integration provides the probability. Total area must equal 1.
section_5.example: A 'Cheat Sheet' graphic overlaying a curve with the equation ∫f(x)dx = 1, reinforcing the fundamental rule of total probability.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text("- " + line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF33FF")
        self.play(Create(area))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        label = MathTex("P(2 < X < 3)").next_to(area, UP)

        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "PDF is a density, not a probability.",
            "Integration calculates probability from density functions.",
            "Total area must always equal one."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Key Takeaways", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        pdf_def = Text("f(x) = Density", font_size=32)
        prob_int = MathTex(r"\int_{a}^{b} f(x) dx = P(a < X < b)", font_size=32)
